T: A boy, a pelican and the Coorong.
D: A boy living with his reclusive dad on the wild South Australian coast raises an orphaned pelican called Mr Percival.
P: Serve the fish when Hideaway Tom brings in the catch.
S: Coorong smoked mullet pâté on toast
Smoked mullet whipped with cream cheese and lemon, piled on hot toast.

Flake 400g smoked mullet fillets (smoked trout works too) off the skin and bones. Beat with 150g softened cream cheese, 2 tbsp sour cream, the zest and juice of 1 lemon, 1 bunch of chopped chives and plenty of black pepper until creamy but still rough. Toast 8 slices of sourdough and serve with sliced cucumber and lemon wedges.
Pipis steamed open in garlic, chilli, lemon butter, with crusty bread

Pipis steamed open with garlic, chilli and a splash of stock, finished with butter, lemon and parsley and served with crusty bread. Soak 1kg pipis in cold salted water for 1 hour to purge the sand, then rinse. Fry 3 sliced garlic cloves and 1 sliced red chilli in 2 tbsp olive oil for 1 minute. Add the pipis and 100ml fish stock, cover and steam 3 to 4 minutes until they open, discarding any that stay shut. Stir in 30g butter, the juice of 1 lemon and chopped parsley. Serve with crusty bread.
M: Hideaway Tom's crisp fish and chips
Battered white fish with chicken salt chips and homemade tartare

Crisp battered fish fillets with thick chips, lemon, tartare sauce and chicken salt, eaten out of paper like at the shack. Bake 1kg frozen thick-cut chips at 220C for 30 minutes. Whisk 150g plain flour, 1 tsp baking powder and 250ml cold soda water into a batter. Dust 4 firm white fish fillets in flour, dip in the batter and fry at 180C for 5 minutes until golden. Mix 150g mayonnaise with chopped capers, pickles and dill for tartare. Toss the chips in chicken salt and serve wrapped in paper with lemon.
W: Apples baked soft with honey, sultanas and cinnamon, with cream.

Core 4 large Granny Smith apples and score a line around the middle of each. Stand them in a baking dish, fill with a mix of 60g sultanas, 40g softened butter, 3 tbsp honey and 1 tsp cinnamon, pour 100ml hot water into the dish and bake at 180C for 45 minutes, spooning the juices over twice, until soft. Serve warm with cream.
K: Coorong shack black tea with honey
Strong black tea with honey and milk, poured hot from the pot.
Boil 1.2 litres of water, pour it over 6 black tea bags in a large teapot and steep for 4 minutes. Stir in 4 tbsp honey, pour into mugs and serve with 300ml of warm milk on the side.

s.note: Tiny fish, crumbed and fried, with lemon. Three hungry chicks would clear the plate.

d.n: Lemon cordial in a tin mug
d.note: Lemon cordial poured in a tin mug. The drink of a boy named Storm Boy.

dishes.n: Coorong smoked mullet pâté on toast
dishes.make_ahead: Make the pâté up to 1 day ahead and keep it covered in the fridge; toast just before serving

steps.text: Flake the smoked mullet into a bowl, taking out every bone and the skin.
Beat in the cream cheese, sour cream, lemon zest and juice, chives and pepper until creamy but rough.
Toast the sourdough, slice the cucumber and cut the lemon into wedges.
Pile the pâté on the toast and serve with cucumber and lemon.

veg.n: Smoked eggplant and white bean pâté on toast (vegetarian)

steps.text: Prick the eggplants and roast whole at 220C until they collapse.
Scoop out the flesh and blend with the beans, oil, lemon zest and juice, paprika and a pinch of salt until rough.
Toast the sourdough, slice the cucumber and chop the chives.
Pile the pâté on the toast and serve with cucumber and chives.

veg.make_ahead: Make the pâté up to 1 day ahead and keep it covered in the fridge; toast just before serving

dishes.make_ahead: Soak the pipis in cold salted water up to 2 hours ahead, then rinse; cook just before serving

steps.text: Soak the pipis in cold salted water to purge the sand, then rinse.
Slice the garlic and chilli.
Fry the garlic and chilli in olive oil.
Add the pipis and fish stock, cover and steam until they open, discarding any that stay shut.
Stir in butter, lemon juice and parsley.
Serve with crusty bread.

ingredients.item: mixed mushrooms, such as Swiss brown and shiitake

steps.text: Tear or thickly slice the mushrooms.
Slice the garlic and chilli.
Fry the mushrooms in the olive oil over high heat until golden.
Add the garlic and chilli and fry for a minute.
Add the stock, cover and steam briefly.
Stir in butter, lemon juice and parsley.
Serve with crusty bread.

dishes.n: Hideaway Tom's crisp fish and chips

steps.text: Bake the chips at 220C.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and cold soda water into a batter.
Dust the fish fillets in flour and dip in the batter.
Fry in the vegetable oil at 180C until golden.
Mix the mayonnaise with chopped capers, pickles and dill for tartare.
Toss the chips in chicken salt and serve wrapped in paper with lemon.

veg.n: Hideaway Tom's crisp banana blossom and chips

ingredients.item: cans banana blossom in brine (about 510 g each), drained

steps.text: Bake the chips at 220C.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and cold soda water into a batter, keeping a little flour back.
Pat the banana blossom dry and press into 8 fillet shapes. Sprinkle with the nori, dust in the saved flour and dip in the batter.
Fry in the oil at 180C until golden.
Mix the mayonnaise with chopped capers, pickles and dill for tartare.
Toss the chips in the celery salt and paprika and serve wrapped in paper with lemon.

dishes.make_ahead: Stuff the apples up to 4 hours ahead; bake just before dinner

steps.text: Core the apples and score a line around the middle of each.
Mix the sultanas, butter, honey and cinnamon and pack into the apples.
Stand the apples in a dish with the hot water and bake at 180C, spooning the juices over twice.
Rest 5 minutes and serve warm with cream.

dishes.n: Coorong shack black tea with honey

steps.text: Boil the water and pour it over the tea bags in a large pot.
Steep for 4 minutes, stir in the honey and warm the milk.
Pour into mugs and serve with the milk on the side.
